agent_record.title: Configure Application
agent_record.scope: The target 'Configure Application' encompasses behavioral obligations where the User interacts with the HATS-GUI to modify, view, or manage application configuration settings. This includes accessing the Configure menu, entering values for specific configuration elements (editors, node display attributes, file associations, HATS-SML paths), and saving these configurations. It explicitly excludes general file management (create/delete files not related to config), transformation execution, parsing, or output viewing, unless they directly involve setting or using configuration parameters defined in the application configuration.

agent_record.title: Display the full text of a publication
agent_record.primary_actor: VUB-network users and Members , Publishers, Moderators and Administrators
agent_record.scope: Target T003 'Display the full text of a publication'. In scope: system capability to store and access/display full text (PDF/Postscript) when available; role-based permissions to download/access content; export formats for results. Exclusions: bibliographic metadata search mechanics, account management, upload/edit functions (except as they gate access), and administrative controls not directly enabling text display.
interpretation_rules: Interpret 'Display' broadly to include 'accessing contents' and 'downloading/exporting' as defined in SRC-001 and SRC-004, since the source does not distinguish between inline viewing and file retrieval for the core obligation.
Restrict obligations to those explicitly granting or denying access to publication content (full text/abstract) or defining the formats in which that content is made available.
Exclude obligations related to modifying publication data (upload/edit) or managing user accounts, as these are administrative prerequisites rather than the act of displaying text itself.
alternatives_and_dissent: One could argue that 'Display' strictly means inline browser rendering, excluding 'Download'. However, SRC-001 links 'accessing contents' with 'save entire text', and SRC-004 lists 'Export and Download' under Result Functions for search queries, implying these are the primary mechanisms for users to obtain/view the full text. Therefore, download/export capabilities are included as essential to 'Display' in this context.

RB008 (VUB-Network User cannot upload/edit) was excluded because it restricts modification rights, not access/display rights. VUB-Network Users *can* download (R003), so their ability to 'display' is confirmed elsewhere.

agent_record.title: Modify Use Case
agent_record.scope: The target is the 'Modify Use Case' for the Unified University Inventory System (UUIS), focusing on the functional requirements for editing and modifying existing inventory assets. This includes the permissions required to perform these actions (who can edit within their scope), constraints on which fields can be modified, and supported methods such as bulk entry. It explicitly excludes transferring assets, adding new assets, creating locations, or managing borrowing requests, as these are distinct operations listed separately in the source.
interpretation_rules: Interpret 'Editing Assets' (5.2) and 'Modifying assets' (5.3) as a single cohesive use case for changing asset data, as the source uses 'edit' and 'modify' interchangeably (e.g., 'asset:edit and modify', 'in order to make modification').

Split obligations by actor scope (Department, Faculty, University) where the source explicitly distinguishes them ('same thing for faculty user...'), to ensure independent testability of permission boundaries.
Treat 'bulk entry' as a capability within the modification use case, not a separate use case, as it is listed under section 5.3.

Permission/role statements (R006-R014) are confirmed only as conditions that gate who may edit; they are not independent use-case actions and do not require describing every permission in the catalog.
Exclude general authorization statements that are fully covered by specific role-based permissions to avoid redundancy.
alternatives_and_dissent: One could argue that 'Editing' and 'Modifying' are distinct steps (e.g., initiating edit vs. saving changes), but the source treats them under the same logical flow of updating asset data, with 5.3 defining constraints on the action described in 5.2.

One could include 'Transferring Assets' as part of modification since it updates location/ownership, but the source lists it as a separate operation (5.1) with distinct approval workflows, so it is excluded from this specific 'Modify' target.

Alternative: exclude R006-R014 as background permission catalog rather than use-case obligations. Rejected because these conditions directly determine who may perform the edit action for this target; they are confirmed as gating conditions, not as separate actions.

agent_record.title: Notify join/leave multicast group
agent_record.scope: The target 'Notify join/leave multicast group' is interpreted as the system's behavioral obligations regarding the management of multicast group membership by agents within the agentMom framework.
